title: Adopted trivial-potential classical charged scalar model

items.title: Adopted trivial-potential classical charged scalar model
items.physical_scope: A classical C2 complex scalar on a C3 Lorentzian metric, including the smooth subclass, with a globally defined real C2 electromagnetic potential A and exact field strength F=dA, arbitrary real coupling lambda, positive scalar normalization K_phi, and smooth real self-potential V. This is the trivial-potential sector only; it is not a quantum, empirical, material-response, or coupled-solution claim.

references.title: David Tong, Gauge Theory, complete author-hosted lecture notes (457-page PDF)
references.locator: §2.5.2, PDF pp. 89–91 (printed pp. 78–80): the four-dimensional Abelian-Higgs action and its charged complex scalar covariant derivative. Only the classical functional form is used; its natural units, Higgs potential, superconducting interpretation, and quantum material claims are not imported.

references.title: H. Friedrich and A. D. Rendall, The Cauchy Problem for the Einstein Equations, Lecture Notes in Physics 540 (2000), complete 97-page preprint
references.locator: §3.1, PDF pp. 22–31, and §5.4, PDF pp. 81–87: the symmetric-hyperbolic local Cauchy framework and Einstein–matter coupling, including brief charged-scalar context. The source gives no complete proof for this exact coupled system.

references.title: Sean M. Carroll, Lecture Notes on General Relativity, arXiv:gr-qc/9712019v1 (1997), complete 238-page lecture notes
references.locator: Ch. 4, eqs. (4.68)–(4.70), PDF pp. 123–124 (printed pp. 117–118), matter action and Hilbert-stress conventions; Ch. 5, eqs. (5.33)–(5.38), PDF p. 145 (printed p. 139), on-shell diffeomorphism identity. Its units and signs are not adopted.

items.statement:
Use a smooth Hausdorff, second-countable underlying oriented four-manifold
with a time-oriented $C^3$ Lorentzian metric, signature
$(-,+,+,+)$, Levi-Civita connection, curvature convention, and SI length-coordinate
units of [[def-emg-geometry-units]]. Use the explicit classical domain of [[def-emg-classical-charged-scalar-finite-regularity-system]]. Let $A$ be a $C^2$, globally defined real
one-form with components in tesla-metres, and set $F:=dA$, so $F$ is a $C^1$
exact real two-form. The globally defined potential is the selected
**trivial-potential sector**: it excludes bundles with no global potential and
does not impose an integer charge condition.

Let $\varphi:M\to\mathbb C$ be a $C^2$ dimensionless classical scalar field. Smooth configurations remain a subclass.
Choose $\lambda\in\mathbb R$ with units $(\mathrm{T\,m^2})^{-1}$, a constant
$K_\varphi>0$ with units $\mathrm{J\,m^{-1}}$, and an open set
$\mathcal U\subseteq\mathbb R$ containing the range of $|\varphi|^2$ together
with a smooth real function $V:\mathcal U\to\mathbb R$ whose values are in
$\mathrm{m^{-2}}$. No sign, polynomial-degree, or smallness condition is
imposed on $V$.

Define the gauge-covariant scalar derivative and charged covector by
$P_a:=D_a\varphi:=\partial_a\varphi-i\lambda A_a\varphi$. For a charged
covector $P_b$, define $D_aP_b:=\nabla_aP_b-i\lambda A_aP_b$, where $\nabla$
is the Levi-Civita derivative, and set $D^aP_a:=g^{ab}D_aP_b$. The adopted
classical matter action is

$$S_\varphi[g,A,\varphi]= -\frac{K_\varphi}{2c}\int_M\left(g^{ab}\overline{P_a}P_b+V(|\varphi|^2)\right)\mathrm{vol}_g.$$

With the stated SI dimensions, $S_\varphi$ has unit joule-second. For a gauge
function $\chi$ in $A\mapsto A+d\chi$, assign $[\chi]=\mathrm{T\,m^2}=\mathrm{Wb}$,
so $d\chi$ has the same unit as the components of $A$ and $\lambda\chi$ is
dimensionless.

On a noncompact domain the integral is used when finite; otherwise the
formulation concerns compactly supported action differences. Variations are
smooth and compactly supported in the fixed global-potential sector. Adopt this
functional as a classical matter model. In particular, this item does not
assert that the model describes nature, that its coupled equations have a
solution, or that the scalar is a quantum field.

The scalar action is adopted in this global real-potential domain. The
Einstein–Hilbert and free Maxwell coefficients below agree with the smooth
action convention of [[post-emg-einstein-maxwell-action]], but the present
model is declared directly: an arbitrary real $\lambda$ is not required to
define an integer-weight representation of a principal circle bundle.
For the declared classical class, separately adopt the same total functional on the domain and compact smooth directions of [[def-emg-classical-charged-scalar-finite-regularity-system]]:

$$S_{\mathrm{tot}}=\frac{c^3}{16\pi G_N}\int_M(R-2\Lambda)\,\mathrm{vol}_g-\frac{1}{4\mu_0c}\int_MF_{ab}F^{ab}\,\mathrm{vol}_g+S_\varphi.$$

Every integral here is a relative compact action when a global integral is not finite. Adopt independent stationarity for all smooth compact symmetric inverse-metric, real one-form and complex scalar directions. [[lem-emg-classical-charged-scalar-compact-variation]] proves all first variations and their pointwise equation equivalence at $g\in C^3$, $A,\varphi\in C^2$. This declares the classical action model, including all its smooth configurations, without requiring a circle-bundle matter representation. The separate smooth circle-sector action formulation is not a prerequisite for this global-real-potential branch.

Its gauge action is
$A\mapsto A+d\chi$, $\varphi\mapsto e^{i\lambda\chi}\varphi$ for a smooth
real function $\chi$; direct substitution gives
$D'_a\varphi'=e^{i\lambda\chi}D_a\varphi$, so the scalar action density is
gauge invariant. It is also invariant under orientation-preserving
diffeomorphisms because its integrand is a scalar multiplied by the metric
volume form. These are properties of the selected functional, not evidence
that it describes nature.

For clarity, the mathematical supplier [[lem-emg-charged-scalar-variation]]
gives the compact first variations and defines

$$E_\varphi:=D^aP_a-V'(|\varphi|^2)\varphi,\qquad j^a:=K_\varphi\lambda\operatorname{Im}(\overline\varphi P^a),$$

$$T^\varphi_{ab}:=K_\varphi\operatorname{Re}(\overline{P_a}P_b)-\frac{K_\varphi}{2}g_{ab}\left(g^{cd}\overline{P_c}P_d+V(|\varphi|^2)\right).$$

Here $E_\varphi=0$ is the scalar Euler–Lagrange equation, $j$ is the current
from varying $A$, and $T^\varphi$ is the Hilbert stress tensor from varying the
inverse metric. Those formulas are mathematical consequences of the action
under the cited supplier's hypotheses; they are not extra physical laws. For smooth fields those formulas use the cited smooth variation result; for the declared classical fields the identical formulas and compact stationarity equivalence are proved in [[lem-emg-classical-charged-scalar-compact-variation]]. Both are mathematical deductions, separate from adoption of the physical model.

items.title: Local evolution of the adopted classical charged scalar model
items.physical_scope: Conditional local existence and smooth local uniqueness, up to spacetime isometry and electromagnetic gauge, for the adopted Einstein–Maxwell–classical charged-scalar action in the global real-potential sector and for the stated compatible initial data, with the finite-Sobolev branch interpreted in the explicit classical C3-metric/C2-matter action domain. The deduction uses the current draft mathematical development result with its exact Countable Choice and Dependent Choice assumptions. It asserts no empirical validity, quantum interpretation, nontrivial bundle sector, singular-source evolution, global existence, or geodesic completeness.

items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ and Dependent Choice (DC). No
stronger choice principle is assumed. Use a smooth Hausdorff, second-countable,
boundaryless, oriented underlying four-manifold with a time-oriented $C^3$
Lorentzian metric $(M,g,N,o)$, signature $(-,+,+,+)$,
curvature convention, length coordinates $x^0=ct$, and SI assignments of
[[def-emg-geometry-units]]. Fix $c,G_N,\mu_0,K_\varphi>0$,
$\lambda,\Lambda\in\mathbb R$, and a real $V\in C^\infty(\mathcal U)$ on an
open interval $\mathcal U\subseteq\mathbb R$ containing the attained values
of $|\varphi|^2$. The classical domain is [[def-emg-classical-charged-scalar-finite-regularity-system]]: the model uses a $C^2$ complex scalar $\varphi$ and a
globally defined real $C^2$ one-form $A$ with $F=dA$. The smooth configurations are retained as a subclass. In length coordinates
$[A_a]=\mathrm{Wb\,m^{-1}}$, $[\lambda]=\mathrm{Wb^{-1}}$,
$[K_\varphi]=\mathrm{J\,m^{-1}}$, and $[V]=\mathrm{m^{-2}}$.

Adopt the explicit classical compact-interior stationary total action of
[[post-emg-trivial-classical-charged-scalar-model]]. The same declared classical action includes smooth configurations; no integer-weight circle representation is assumed for arbitrary real $\lambda$.
Write $\mathcal D_a\varphi:=\partial_a\varphi-i\lambda A_a\varphi$ and
$P_a:=\mathcal D_a\varphi$. For a charged covector set
$\mathcal D_aP_b:=\nabla_aP_b-i\lambda A_aP_b$, where $\nabla$ is the
spacetime Levi-Civita derivative; indices are raised with $g^{-1}$. The scalar
equation, current and Hilbert tensor are

$$E_\varphi:=\mathcal D_aP^a-V'(|\varphi|^2)\varphi=0,\qquad j^a:=K_\varphi\lambda\operatorname{Im}(\overline\varphi P^a),$$

$$T^\varphi_{ab}:=K_\varphi\operatorname{Re}(\overline{P_a}P_b)-\frac{K_\varphi}{2}g_{ab}\bigl(g^{cd}\overline{P_c}P_d+V(|\varphi|^2)\bigr).$$

Set $T^{\mathrm{EM}}_{ab}:=\mu_0^{-1}(F_{ac}F_b{}^c-\tfrac14g_{ab}F_{cd}F^{cd})$,
$T^{\mathrm{tot}}:=T^{\mathrm{EM}}+T^\varphi$, and
$\kappa_E:=8\pi G_N/c^4$. The equations of the adopted action model are

$$dF=0,\qquad \nabla_aF^{ab}=-\mu_0j^b,\qquad G_{ab}+\Lambda g_{ab}=\kappa_E T^{\mathrm{tot}}_{ab},\qquad E_\varphi=0.$$

Let $\Sigma$ be a smooth spacelike initial hypersurface, $h$ its induced
Riemannian metric, $n$ its future unit normal, and
$\mathcal K(X,Y):=g(\nabla_Xn,Y)$ its second fundamental form. Let
$\nabla^\Sigma$ denote the Levi-Civita derivative of $h$ and
$\tau:=\operatorname{tr}_h\mathcal K$.
Let $i_\Sigma:\Sigma\hookrightarrow M$ be the inclusion. The complete scalar
data are $\varphi_0:=\varphi|_\Sigma$,
$\pi_i:=(\mathcal D_i\varphi)|_\Sigma$, and the independently prescribed
$\pi_n:=n^a\mathcal D_a\varphi|_\Sigma$. In a spatial chart this means
$\pi_i=\partial_i\varphi_0-i\lambda A_{\Sigma,i}\varphi_0$. The globally
defined spatial potential is $A_\Sigma:=i_\Sigma^*A$, with exact-potential
compatibility $F|_{T\Sigma}=d_\Sigma A_\Sigma$. Use the temporal potential
gauge $A_0:=A(\partial_0)=0$ in local normal coordinates with $\partial_0=n$
initially, so $A(n)=0$ on $\Sigma$ and $\pi_0=\pi_n$ initially.

For the periodic high-regularity branch take
$\Sigma=\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}:=\mathbb R^3/(2\pi\mathbb Z)^3$ with
dimensionless periodic coordinates $y^i$, and fix $L_0>0$ metres so that the
length coordinates are $x^i=L_0y^i$. Sobolev norms use $y$; tensor components
and derivative units use the length coordinates $x$. Let $s\ge5$ be an integer. Prescribe a
Riemannian metric $h\in H^{s+1}$ whose continuous
representative satisfies $h\ge c_0I$ for some $c_0>0$, a symmetric
$\mathcal K\in H^s$, spatial vector fields $e,b\in H^s$, a global real
$A_\Sigma\in H^s$, $\varphi_0\in H^{s+1}$, and an independent complex
$\pi_n\in H^s$. Here the Sobolev spaces are componentwise real, with complex
components split into real and imaginary parts. For the periodic state, let
$(\mathsf e_A(h))_{A=1}^3$ be the positively oriented $h$-orthonormal frame
obtained by Gram–Schmidt from the ordered global length-coordinate frame, as
specified in [[def-emg-periodic-high-sobolev-state]]. Put
$\widehat e_A:=h(e,\mathsf e_A(h))$ and
$\widehat b_A:=h(b,\mathsf e_A(h))$. The initial two-form convention below
then gives $F_\Sigma(\mathsf e_A(h),n)=\widehat e_A$ and
$F_\Sigma(\mathsf e_A(h),\mathsf e_B(h))=\epsilon_{ABC}\widehat b_C$, with
$\epsilon_{123}=+1$. Thus $\widehat e_A=E_A/c$ and
$\widehat b_A=B_A$ in the observer convention of [[def-emg-geometry-units]],
and both components have unit tesla. Sobolev regularity of the vector fields
$e,b$ refers to their components in the fixed periodic coordinates; the
orthonormal-frame state components are those specified by the named convention.
The initial two-form $F_\Sigma$ is fixed by
$F_\Sigma(X,n)=h(e,X)$ and
$F_\Sigma(X,Y)=\mathrm{vol}_h(b,X,Y)$ for spatial $X,Y$. Assume
$\pi_i=\mathcal D_i\varphi_0$ and
$F_\Sigma|_{T\Sigma}=d_\Sigma A_\Sigma$. With $j,T^{\mathrm{tot}}$
evaluated on the complete initial fields, impose the Maxwell constraints

$$\nabla^\Sigma_i b^i=0,\qquad \nabla^\Sigma_i e^i=\mu_0j^0,\qquad j^0:=-n_aj^a,$$

and the Einstein constraints in the stated sign convention,

$$R(h)+\tau^2-|\mathcal K|_h^2=2\Lambda+2\kappa_E T^{\mathrm{tot}}(n,n),\qquad (\operatorname{div}_h\mathcal K)(X)-\nabla^\Sigma_X\tau=\kappa_E T^{\mathrm{tot}}(n,X)\quad(X\in T\Sigma).$$

Here $(\operatorname{div}_h\mathcal K)(X):=h^{ij}(\nabla^\Sigma_{\partial_i}\mathcal K)(\partial_j,X)$, so the momentum equation is an equality of covectors and does not mix coordinate and orthonormal components.

Fix a smooth positive reference metric $\gamma$ on $\Sigma$ and the product
comparison metric $\bar g:=-(dx^0)^2+\gamma$ near the initial slice. Define
$H^a:=g^{bc}(\Gamma(g)^a{}_{bc}-\Gamma(\bar g)^a{}_{bc})$ and
$Q^i:=h^{jk}(\Gamma(h)^i{}_{jk}-\Gamma(\gamma)^i{}_{jk})$. Use the initial
harmonic metric jet

$$g_{ij}=h_{ij},\quad g_{00}=-1,\quad g_{0i}=0,\quad \partial_0g_{ij}=2\mathcal K_{ij},\quad \partial_0g_{00}=-2\tau,\quad \partial_0g_{0i}=h_{ij}Q^j.$$

Let $\bar\nabla$ be the Levi-Civita derivative of $\bar g$ and put
$p_{ab}:=\bar\nabla_0g_{ab}$ and $q_{abi}:=\bar\nabla_i g_{ab}$ for the
first-order metric derivative variables. For a fixed field scale $F_0>0$
tesla, form the real first-order state from
$(g_{ab},p_{ab},q_{abi})$, the six orthonormal-frame Maxwell components
$(\widehat e_A,\widehat b_A)$, the three spatial potential components $A_i$,
and the real and imaginary parts of $\varphi,\pi_0,\pi_i$. Rescale each first
metric derivative and each $\pi_a$ by multiplying by $L_0$, each
$\widehat e_A,\widehat b_A$ by dividing by $F_0$, and each $A_i$ by dividing
by $L_0F_0$; $g_{ab}$ and $\varphi$ are already
dimensionless. These fixed invertible scales are bookkeeping choices, not
extra equations. Denote the resulting componentwise-real periodic state by
$u_0$. Suppose its continuous range is a compact $K_0$ contained in the
interior of a compact $K_1$ inside an open admissible state set $O$, that the
coefficient maps are smooth on $O$, the potential range lies in $\mathcal U$,
and the combined time matrix is positive definite throughout $O$. Require
$\|u_0\|_{H^s}\le R$ for some finite $R\ge0$. Thus
$u_0\in\mathcal S_s(K_0,R)$ in the componentwise real periodic Fourier and
weak-derivative convention used by the CP04 supplier.

Under the stated mathematical hypotheses of the current authored supplier
[[thm-emg-local-classical-charged-scalar-development]], these periodic data
have a local solution of the full Einstein, sourced
Maxwell, and classical charged-scalar equations on
$(-T_*,T_*)\times\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}$. Here $T_*>0$ is a width in the length
coordinate $x^0=ct$ (so the corresponding time width in seconds is $T_*/c$).
In its coordinate gauge, the first-order state lies in
$L^\infty H^s\cap C H^{s-1}$ with time derivative in
$L^\infty H^{s-1}$; the metric has
$g\in L^\infty H^{s+1}\cap C H^s$ and
$\partial_0g\in L^\infty H^s\cap C H^{s-1}$, while
$F,\pi,A_i\in L^\infty H^s\cap C H^{s-1}$ and
$\varphi\in L^\infty H^{s+1}\cap C H^s$. The Maxwell, scalar-potential,
metric-derivative, and harmonic constraints propagate. More generally, for
smooth data $(h,\mathcal K,e,b,A_\Sigma,\varphi_0,\pi_n)$ on any smooth
oriented three-manifold without boundary, define $F_\Sigma$ by
$F_\Sigma(X,n)=h(e,X)$ and
$F_\Sigma(X,Y)=\mathrm{vol}_h(b,X,Y)$ for spatial $X,Y$. The current authored supplier states local smooth development near each initial point, provided
$h$ is positive definite, $A_\Sigma$ is global,
$F_\Sigma|_{T\Sigma}=d_\Sigma A_\Sigma$,
$\pi_i=\mathcal D_i\varphi_0$, $A(n)=0$, the sourced Maxwell and
total-stress Einstein constraints hold, and $|\varphi|^2$ remains in
$\mathcal U$. Its uniqueness conclusion is local near the initial surface, up
to a data-fixing time-orientation-preserving isometry and electromagnetic
gauge $A\mapsto A+d\chi$,
$\varphi\mapsto e^{i\lambda\chi}\varphi$ with $\chi|_\Sigma=0$ and
$[\chi]=\mathrm{Wb}$. This is a local conditional deduction in the adopted action
model. It asserts no nontrivial bundle sector, singular source, global-in-time
existence, geodesic completeness, empirical validity, or quantum field.

items.physical_scope: Exact zero-scalar reduction of the classical finite-regularity trivial-potential charged-scalar model when V(0)=0. It is a conditional model calculation with no empirical, quantum, or nontrivial-bundle claim.

items.statement:
Let $U$ be an open region of a smooth Hausdorff, second-countable, oriented
underlying four-manifold with a time-oriented $C^3$ Lorentzian metric $g$ of
signature $(-,+,+,+)$. Let $A$ be a $C^2$ global
real one-form on $U$ and set $F:=dA$. Assume the source-free Einstein–Maxwell
equations of [[pthm-emg-classical-charged-scalar-model-evolution]] hold on $U$:
$$dF=0,\qquad \nabla_aF^{ab}=0,\qquad G_{ab}+\Lambda g_{ab}=\kappa_E T^{\mathrm{EM}}_{ab},\qquad T^{\mathrm{EM}}_{ab}=\mu_0^{-1}\left(F_{ac}F_b{}^c-\frac14g_{ab}F_{cd}F^{cd}\right).$$
Let $V$ be smooth on an open set containing $0$, with $V(0)=0$, and set
$\varphi\equiv0$ on $U$. Then $\varphi$ is an exact solution of the adopted
classical charged-scalar model coupled to this Einstein–Maxwell field: its
current and Hilbert stress vanish, so the full equations reduce to the stated
source-free equations. For Cauchy data satisfying the hypotheses of
[[pthm-emg-classical-charged-scalar-model-evolution]] and additionally
$\varphi_0=0$ and $\pi_n=0$, the zero field is the corresponding local branch
under that theorem's stated mathematical hypotheses and the adopted model.
